findings.location: Section "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide"
findings.evidence: "This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise."
findings.violation: The assertion that no library that has tried ending fines has found otherwise is presented without evidence or citations to support such a broad generalization.
findings.fix: Either cite sources from other libraries' experiences with fine elimination, or reframe the claim as "Our pilot data supports this approach" rather than claiming universal consistency.

findings.evidence: The section begins by identifying the concern about "a shortfall the consortium has not planned for" but then states "The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring."
findings.violation: The section identifies but does not actually address the revenue concern about materials-replacement funding. The renovation project schedule is unrelated to the materials-replacement funding question.
findings.fix: Either provide actual analysis of where the funding gap will be filled (alternative revenue sources, budget reallocation, adjusted collection policies) or remove this incomplete section.

findings.location: Section "What the Pilot Showed", paragraph about patron survey
findings.evidence: "A parallel patron survey found that self-reported avoidance of the library due to fear of fines dropped from 22 percent of respondents before the pilot to 5 percent after it... The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.violation: The survey was only administered at pilot branches, so it provides no data on whether avoidance due to fear of fines changed at the non-pilot branches that kept fines.
findings.fix: Add data from non-pilot branches in the same survey period to show whether fine-related avoidance is a problem systemwide, or clarify that this benefit applies only to the specific branches tested.

findings.location: Section "What the Pilot Showed", first paragraph
findings.evidence: "During an 18-month pilot at 5 branches, the on-time-or-eventual return rate for borrowed items held at 93 percent, compared with 86 percent at the branches that kept fines in place over the same period."
findings.violation: The document does not establish whether the five pilot branches are comparable to the control branches in size, location, demographics, or collection composition, so it is unclear whether a 7-percentage-point improvement is generalizable.
findings.fix: Describe the characteristics of the pilot branches and control branches (size, location, collection type, patron demographics) to establish comparability, or acknowledge this as a limitation.

findings.location: Section "What the Pilot Showed", first paragraph
findings.evidence: "Materials-recovery staff logged the comparison monthly using the same circulation software used consortium-wide."
findings.violation: The sentence does not clearly explain what "the comparison" means or what method was used to verify the difference in return rates.
findings.fix: Specify the exact metric being tracked (on-time returns vs. eventual returns vs. all returns), the method used to identify and count items in each category, and how the staff ensured consistency across branches.

findings.evidence: Document ends after incomplete sentence fragment in "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section.
findings.violation: The recommendation document appears incomplete; the final section addressing the board's revenue concern does not reach a conclusion.
findings.fix: Complete the analysis in the "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section to address how the consortium will handle the potential revenue loss from eliminated fines.
